title: The barrel boom before the transition
gist: Oxford Economics raised its 2030 African oil output forecast to nearly 8.2 mbpd (up about 930,000 bpd) after a methodology upgrade, yet Africa's share of global supply only edges up to 7.8%. Growth comes from Nigeria plus frontier producers like Egypt, while African oil demand is projected to grow 2.7% a year versus 0.4% globally.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics now expects African oil output to reach nearly 8.2 million barrels per day by 2030, about 930,000 bpd above its previous projection, following a broader upgrade to its oil forecast methodology; Africa's share of global supply rises only slightly, to 7.8%.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: An upward revision of nearly 1 mbpd in a single continent's supply is a bearish nudge for the oil balance, though the small share gain limits its global price impact.
insights.quote: we now expect cumulative continental output to reach nearly 8.2 million barrels per day (mbpd) by 2030
insights.locator: We've comprehensively reviewed our oil production predictions

insights.claim: The four largest African producers (Nigeria, Angola, Algeria, Libya) are expected to add only about 460,000 bpd by 2030, with Nigeria leading at 1.8 mbpd, while emerging producers led by Egypt and other frontier nations are anticipated to supply nearly 2.5 mbpd collectively.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Roughly half of the upgrade comes from incumbents and the rest from frontier names, so the supply story is a broadening one and depends on newer, less-proven producers.
insights.quote: showcasing a shift in the oil landscape

insights.claim: African oil demand is projected to grow 2.7% per annum between 2024 and 2030, well above the 0.4% global average, even as global oil demand faces structural decline, which Oxford Economics frames as an opportunity for African producers.
insights.speaker: Keith Mason
insights.so_what: Growing local demand could absorb more of the continent's output domestically, which would reduce export volumes and could change trade flows.
insights.quote: continental demand is projected to grow at 2.7% per annum between 2024 and 2030, significantly outpacing the global average of 0.4%
insights.locator: While Africa continues to exploit its oil resources
